scout.name: Kane CLI Online Hackathon

prizes.other: Kane CLI swag for top 10 teams

scout.eligibility: Worldwide, individuals and teams of up to 4, 18 or older. Students, professionals, and independent builders welcome.
scout.notes: Hackathon focuses on agentic QA automation using Kane CLI. Requires a public GitHub repo and a 3-minute screen recording. No camera or personal voice narration required.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The hackathon is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize is $1,500 USD cash.
Solo participation is permitted.
The deadline of 2026-11-19 is in the future relative to the evaluation date.
The submission requirements explicitly state no camera or personal voice narration is required.

risks.risk: The hackathon requires the use of 'Kane CLI', which may imply a proprietary or niche tool that could have hidden learning curves or undocumented limitations affecting project viability.
Prize distribution for international participants (India) may involve complex tax withholding or payment processing fees that could reduce the net value of the $1,500 prize.

builder.idea: Automated Regression Suite for E-commerce using Kane CLI
reuse: Standard boilerplate for CLI-based automation scripts
steps: Install Kane CLI and perform a deep dive into its documentation to map out core capabilities.
Define a target web application (e.g., a mock e-commerce site) to serve as the test subject.
Develop a suite of automated test scripts using Kane CLI to handle user authentication, cart operations, and checkout flows.
Implement a reporting module that exports test results into a clean, readable format.
Record a 3-minute screen capture demonstrating the CLI execution and the resulting test logs.
Prepare the GitHub repository with a clear README, installation instructions, and the demo video.
demo_risks: Unexpected CLI bugs or undocumented command behaviors
Environment configuration issues during the screen recording
Potential latency in the target web application affecting test stability

scout.name: Codegeist 2026
scout.eligibility: Individuals who have reached the age of majority in their jurisdiction; teams allowed. Excludes employees and residents of specific restricted regions (Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea).
scout.notes: Requires a working Forge app or Rovo agent and a public demo video. Screen capture with captions is explicitly permitted, so face/voice recording is not mandatory.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The event is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize is $15,000 USD, which exceeds the $100 minimum.
Solo participation is permitted.
The deadline of 2026-12-22 has not passed.
Face or voice recording is not mandatory.

risks.risk: Atlassian hackathons often require winners to undergo extensive tax documentation and compliance checks, which can be burdensome for international participants.
The requirement for a 'working Forge app or Rovo agent' implies a dependency on Atlassian's proprietary development platform, which may involve steep learning curves or hidden technical constraints.

Prize payments for large corporate hackathons are frequently processed through third-party platforms (like Devpost or similar) which may have specific regional payout limitations or high transaction fees for international bank transfers.

builder.idea: A Rovo Agent for Jira that automates 'Ticket Triage & Contextual Summarization' by pulling data from Confluence and Bitbucket to provide instant resolution suggestions for support engineers.
reuse: Existing boilerplate for Atlassian Forge app authentication
Previous LLM-based summarization logic for technical documentation
Standard screen-capture and video-editing workflow for non-voice demos
steps: Set up Forge development environment and authenticate with Atlassian developer account.
Define Rovo Agent manifest with specific triggers for Jira issue creation.
Implement backend logic to query Confluence pages and Bitbucket PRs related to the issue's component.
Integrate an LLM API (via Forge's external fetch) to synthesize the retrieved context into a concise triage report.
Configure the Agent to post the summary as an internal comment on the Jira ticket.
Record a screen-capture demo with text-based callouts and captions to meet submission requirements.
Finalize documentation and submit via the Codegeist portal.
demo_risks: Forge app latency during API calls to external LLM providers.
Complexity of managing Atlassian's permission scopes for cross-product data access.
Potential for hallucinated triage suggestions if the Rovo Agent context window is poorly constrained.

scout.name: Enveda CASMI 2026
scout.eligibility: Open to Kaggle users worldwide 18 or older, subject to rules and US export controls.
scout.notes: A code competition focused on ranking molecular structures from mass spectrometry data. Participants can compete solo or in teams. Entry is free and open to non-students.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The competition is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize is $16,000 USD, which is a cash prize.
Solo participation is permitted.
The deadline of 2026-12-14 has not passed as of 2026-11-10.
There is no requirement for face or voice recording.

risks.risk: Kaggle prize payment processing for international winners (India) often involves complex tax documentation (W-8BEN) and potential delays or fees from third-party payment processors like Tipalti.

High computational resource requirement: Molecular structure ranking from mass spectrometry data typically requires significant GPU/TPU resources, which may exceed free Kaggle kernel limits, necessitating personal hardware or cloud spend.
Intellectual Property/Licensing: Kaggle competitions often require winners to grant exclusive licenses or transfer IP rights to the sponsor as a condition of prize eligibility.

builder.idea: Enveda CASMI 2026: Deep Learning for Mass Spectrometry Molecular Identification
reuse: Existing PyTorch/GNN boilerplate for molecular graph representation
Pre-trained RDKit pipelines for chemical structure featurization
Kaggle competition submission template (standardized data loader and submission CSV generator)
Cloud-based training scripts (Colab/Kaggle Kernels) for GPU-accelerated model training
steps: Perform Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on mass spectrometry spectra and molecular structure mappings.
Implement a Graph Neural Network (GNN) or Transformer-based architecture to map spectral features to molecular fingerprints.
Develop a robust cross-validation strategy to prevent overfitting on the training set.
Optimize model inference speed to fit within Kaggle's submission time constraints.
Iteratively refine model architecture using ensemble methods and hyperparameter tuning.
Finalize submission pipeline and ensure compliance with Kaggle's code competition requirements.
demo_risks: GPU memory exhaustion during training on large molecular datasets.
Data leakage between training and validation sets due to structural similarities in molecules.
Latency issues during inference if the model architecture is too complex for the competition's time limit.
Potential tax documentation hurdles for international prize disbursement.

scout.name: AI for Church Hackathon
scout.eligibility: Open worldwide to anyone 18 or older.
scout.notes: Submission requires a demo link, writeup, and a 2-3 minute demo video. Screen recording is explicitly permitted, so face/voice is not required.

reasons: The candidate meets all eligibility criteria: it is open to non-students, fully online, free to enter, offers a cash prize exceeding $100, allows solo participation, has a future deadline, and does not require face or voice recording.

risks.risk: Niche domain focus ('AI for Church') may limit the utility of the project outside of the specific religious organization's ecosystem, potentially wasting effort if the project is not generalizable.
Small prize pool ($2,500 total) relative to the effort required for a high-quality demo video and writeup.

builder.idea: SermonSage: An AI-powered sermon analysis and study guide generator that converts audio/text transcripts into structured study materials, discussion questions, and multi-lingual summaries for church small groups.
reuse: Streamlit UI boilerplate for rapid prototyping
steps: Ingest sample sermon transcripts and apply RAG to extract key theological themes and scripture references.
Develop a prompt-chaining module to generate discussion questions and 'take-home' application points.
Build a clean, minimalist Streamlit interface for users to upload files and export study guides as PDFs.
Implement a multi-language translation layer for global accessibility.
Record a screen-capture demo showcasing the workflow from raw audio upload to final study guide generation.
demo_risks: Dependency on high-quality audio transcription accuracy
Potential for 'hallucinated' theological interpretations if prompt engineering is not constrained
Limited visual appeal of a text-heavy tool in a video demo
